result:
No revisit dates have passed. The next one is bake-to-order on 2 Dec 2026.

The free first box is already ruled out (6 October). In September, 52 people took one but only 6 started paying, and the free boxes used Saturday delivery slots. You'd reopen it only if paid signups drop below 8 a month for two months in a row. October had 15, so that hasn't happened. Here's what I'd do instead, best first:

**1. A referral offer through your 140 subscribers (do this first).**
Put a card in every box: "Give a neighbour half off their first month. You get a free week when they stay past month one."
- Half off the first month was also discarded on 6 October, but its reopen condition is exactly this: test it only when the new person comes through an existing subscriber. So this is the approved way to try it, not a repeat of what failed.
- People referred by a neighbour usually live nearby and stay longer than strangers who came for a freebie.
- You only pay the reward once the new subscriber has stayed a month. 10 referrals would cost about €360 in discounts plus 10 free weeks (around €70 in ingredients).
- Track the conversion rate so you can compare it with the 6 out of 52 from the free box.

**2. Paid gift boxes for December (start now, it's 19 November).**
Sell "4 Saturdays of bread" as a Christmas gift for anyone within 3 km. It's paid from week one, so it fits your current pricing decision. It also introduces new households without giving bread away. At the end, invite them to carry on at €18.

**3. Fill the streets you already ride.**
Put door hangers or flyers on the streets around your current subscribers, roughly €80–100 a month. Each new box on an existing route uses very little extra Saturday time, which matters because Saturday is your limit. The cargo bike is free advertising too, so make sure it clearly shows the name and how to sign up.

**4. Partner with neighbouring shops (cheese, wine, deli, coffee).**
Each recommends the other to its customers: a card at their counter, theirs in your box. It costs almost nothing and reaches people who already pay for good food.

**5. Keep the €300 a month mostly for the referral rewards and flyers.**
At this size, paid social ads are the least useful place to spend it.

**Before you push hard:** how many Saturday deliveries can you actually make? If you're near the limit, extra signups turn into a waiting list. That's not bad in itself, and a waiting list helps sell the box. But it changes the plan: you'd want more bike runs or a second rider before adding many more customers. A courier partner is ruled out until you pass 300 subscribers.

If you go ahead with the referral test, tell me and I'll log it. It reopens one of the options you discarded on 6 October, so the ledger should record that.
